audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 1 and 2 disagreed across layers: full-layer phases[].side read Skill for levels 1-3 while content win[] read Orianna for all three.
audit.why: The content layer matches the packet levelChart and the kit. Death's Hand is 750 range against Command: Attack's 815, Nevermove is not available at level 1, and Swain has no dash - so Orianna trades from outside his Q for the first three levels. From 4 the lane evens once Nevermove roots and reels, and soul fragments start healing back the poke.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side -> Orianna at 7/10, whys rewritten in the same proposal to argue the Orianna verdict.

audit.why: Spike placement is right: Swain's real spikes are the level 6 Demonic Ascension drain (120s, 650 range, indefinite while he drains a champion) and first item plus soul stacks turning him into a drain-tank poke cannot kill. Orianna's flip is the two-item teamfight.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly called Swain's root an "E-W root combo" and told you to fear W. It also had no digit in breakdown.cooldowns.
audit.why: Nevermove (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, 850 range) is the ability that roots - the wave travels out, roots on the way back, and he can then pull rooted champions in. Vision of Empire (W) is not a root at all: it is a 22s zone at 5500-7500 range that damages, slows, reveals, and hands him a Soul Fragment. Confusing them tells the reader to dodge the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: whys[3], spikes[0].text, content.mid, wants.foe[0] and wants.you[0] now name Nevermove as the root; breakdown.cooldowns carries 12s/850, 750, and 120s.
sources: brief enemyKit E text and cooldown
brief enemyKit W text and range

audit.whatIsWrong: The single itemisation decision this matchup turns on - Grievous Wounds timing - appeared only as a trailing clause in report[8].t and nowhere in the breakdown fields.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments and permanently raises his maximum health, and Demonic Ascension drains health from every nearby champion, minion and monster. Anti-heal is the mechanical answer, and denying fragments off the wave is the lane-phase version of it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.feeding and breakdown.carry now name Grievous Wounds and fragment denial explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's second missing interaction says Swain bypasses stacking resistances via Ravenous Flock.
audit.why: Riot's passive text says only that ravens collect Soul Fragments which heal him and raise his maximum health. There is no percent-health or resistance-bypass language in it, so the kit file's percentHealth flag is a parsing misfire.
audit.corrected: No edit. That claim was deliberately not written to the page.

notes: The page consistently described an "E-W root combo" and told the reader to fear W. Nevermove (E, 12s, 850) is the root; Vision of Empire (W, 22s, 5500-7500) is a long-range zone that slows, reveals and hands him a Soul Fragment - it does not root. Corrected in whys[3], spikes[0].text, content.mid, wants.foe[0] and wants.you[0]. Cross-layer chart disagreement fixed on rows 0, 1 and 2; win[N] already holds the correct value on disk so no paired edits are proposed. The brief's needs-antiheal interaction IS supported by Riot's passive and R text and is now on the page in breakdown.feeding and breakdown.carry; the resistances-invalidated one is NOT - the passive text has no percent-health or resistance-bypass language, so the kit's percentHealth flag is a misfire and nothing was written from it. The packet's suspectName "Demonic Ascension's" in whys[4] is a false positive: it is a correct possessive of the correct name. Vision of Empire's 5500-7500 range is worth a line somewhere - he can drop it on your wave from off-screen while roaming - but no existing field is a natural home for it at the same length, so it is unwritten; see notes for the QA pass.
